Done. All deliverables are in the working directory.

## What I did

**Dataset:** [DANDI:000044](https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/000044) (Grosmark & Buzsáki 2016, the `hc-11` dataset) — bilateral silicon-probe recordings from dorsal CA1 in four rats running linear tracks. Files are 5–9 GB each; nothing was downloaded in full (`remfile` + `h5py` chunk reads from S3 with a disk cache).

**Two data defects I had to find and handle.** Neither is visible without checking, and either would have silently corrupted the result:

- `SpatialSeries.rate` holds the sampling *period* (0.0256 s), not the frequency. Taking it at face value spreads 80,762 position samples over 36 days. I rebuild the time base and assert it against the MazeEpoch duration.
- In three sessions, the units-table row with id 2 contains two full-session spike trains concatenated end to end, so its spike times jump backwards. Pynapple sorts such a train silently, producing a plausible-looking but meaningless unit. I check the raw ragged array and drop it.

I also excluded the three circular-maze sessions on geometry (a lap wraps around, so the two-direction traversal logic doesn't apply), before looking at any spiking.

## Key result

Across five linear-track sessions (four rats), **211 of 270 putative CA1 pyramidal cells (78%)** qualified as place cells against a circular-shift null that preserves each spike train's own temporal statistics. Median field width 32 cm, peak rate 6.0 Hz, spatial information 0.61 bits/spike — textbook CA1 values.

The strongest evidence is generalization: fitting tuning curves on half the traversals and decoding the other half, **with no place-cell selection**, recovered position to a median error of **5.8–14.1 cm** versus **43–65 cm** for rolled tuning curves, in every session. Independently, a NeMoS Poisson GLM gave a positive held-out pseudo-R² for 94%/90% of place cells but only 18%/6% of other units.

## Files

`hippocampal_place_cells.py` (jupytext, self-contained, runs end-to-end in ~2.5 min), `hippocampal_place_cells.ipynb` (executed, 9 inline figures), 9 PNGs, 3 CSVs, and `README.md`. The modular development scripts (`pf_core.py`, `dandi_io.py`, `fig_*.py`, `multi_session.py`) are kept for reference; the notebook doesn't depend on them.

One caveat worth flagging: the leftward place-cell count shifts by one cell between 200 and 1000 shuffles, which is just boundary sensitivity at p < 0.01 — the notebook uses 1000 for the single-session analysis and 500 for the multi-session sweep.
